query: In the Mailchimp automation unsubscribes data, please show me the automation title, automation status, automation ID, the email's automation ID, the member ID who unsubscribed, and when they unsubscribed? Restrict to automations whose status is sending, and sort the results by unsubscribe time, newest first.
sql:
SELECT
  automation.title,
  automation.status,
  automation.id,
  automation_email.automation_id,
  unsubscribe.member_id,
  unsubscribe.timestamp
FROM automation_email
INNER JOIN unsubscribe ON automation_email.id = unsubscribe.campaign_id
INNER JOIN automation ON automation_email.automation_id = automation.id
WHERE automation.status = 'sending'
ORDER BY unsubscribe.timestamp DESC

query: I'd like to see the count of click actions for each automation that is currently in sending status from the Mailchimp automation data. Group the results by automation ID and status, joining automation emails with their recipient activity records.
sql:
SELECT automation.id AS automation_id, automation.status, COUNT(*) AS count
FROM automation_email
INNER JOIN automation ON automation_email.automation_id = automation.id
INNER JOIN automation_recipient_activity ON automation_email.id = automation_recipient_activity.automation_email_id
WHERE automation_recipient_activity.action = 'click'
  AND automation.status = 'sending'
GROUP BY automation.id, automation.status

query: Show me the recipient list ID, the automation list ID, the member ID, the email title, the automation title, and the automation status for each recipient from the Mailchimp automation recipients data. Restrict to automations whose status is sending.
sql:
SELECT
  automation_recipient.list_id,
  automation.list_id,
  automation_recipient.member_id,
  automation_email.title,
  automation.title,
  automation.status
FROM automation_email
INNER JOIN automation ON automation_email.automation_id = automation.id
INNER JOIN automation_recipient ON automation_email.id = automation_recipient.automation_email_id
WHERE automation.status = 'sending'

query: Using the Zendesk ticket data, could you please show me the brand name, ticket tag, brand ID, ticket ID, and when each ticket was created? Restrict to tickets that are closed, and sort the results by creation date with the newest first.
sql:
SELECT
  brand.name,
  ticket_tag.tag,
  ticket.brand_id,
  ticket_tag.ticket_id,
  ticket.created_at
FROM ticket
INNER JOIN ticket_tag ON ticket.id = ticket_tag.ticket_id
INNER JOIN brand ON ticket.brand_id = brand.id
WHERE ticket.status = 'closed'
ORDER BY ticket.created_at DESC

query: For the Zendesk ticket updates data, please show me the ticket ID, ticket status, the comment's ticket ID, the chat's ticket ID, when the comment was created, and when the chat event was created? Restrict to tickets whose status is closed and whose priority is urgent.
sql:
SELECT
  ticket.id,
  ticket.status,
  ticket_comment.ticket_id,
  ticket_chat.ticket_id,
  ticket_comment.created,
  ticket_chat_event.created_at
FROM ticket
INNER JOIN ticket_comment ON ticket.id = ticket_comment.ticket_id
INNER JOIN ticket_chat ON ticket.id = ticket_chat.ticket_id
INNER JOIN ticket_chat_event ON ticket_chat.chat_id = ticket_chat_event.chat_id
WHERE ticket.status = 'closed'
  AND ticket.priority = 'urgent'

query: From the Zendesk organization data, could you please show me the organization tag, the domain name, the organization ID from both the tag and domain tables, and when the organization was created? Restrict to organizations that have the tag '63ad9d34f3503826e5f649ae6b7ac92c', and sort the results by creation date with the newest first.
sql:
SELECT
  organization_tag.tag,
  domain_name.domain_name,
  organization_tag.organization_id,
  domain_name.organization_id,
  organization.created_at
FROM organization
INNER JOIN organization_tag ON organization.id = organization_tag.organization_id
INNER JOIN domain_name ON organization.id = domain_name.organization_id
WHERE organization_tag.tag = '63ad9d34f3503826e5f649ae6b7ac92c'
ORDER BY organization.created_at DESC

query: Using the Pardot campaigns data, could you please show me the campaign id, campaign name, and campaign cost, and for each related opportunity the campaign id, value, and status, and for each related prospect the campaign ID and prospect id? Please include only the campaign that has the highest id and whose cost equals the maximum cost across all campaigns.
sql:
SELECT
  campaign.id,
  campaign.name,
  campaign.cost,
  opportunity.campaign_id,
  opportunity.value,
  opportunity.status,
  prospect.campaign_id,
  prospect.id
FROM campaign
INNER JOIN opportunity ON campaign.id = opportunity.campaign_id
INNER JOIN prospect ON campaign.id = prospect.campaign_id
WHERE campaign.id = (
    SELECT MAX(c.id)
    FROM campaign c
    WHERE c.id IN (SELECT campaign_id FROM opportunity)
      AND c.id IN (SELECT campaign_id FROM prospect)
  )
  AND COALESCE(TRY_CAST(campaign.cost AS DOUBLE), -999999.0) = (SELECT COALESCE(MAX(TRY_CAST(cost AS DOUBLE)), -999999.0) FROM campaign)

query: Using the pendo data, the query retrieves data by joining the event, feature_event, and page_event tables on the account_id column. It selects the account_id, num_events, and num_minutes columns from the event table, the account_id and num_events columns from the feature_event table, and the account_id and num_events columns from the page_event table. Additionally, it calculates a new column num_events_filled using the COALESCE function to fill event.num_events with 0 if it is NULL. The query filters the results to include only those records from the event table where the timestamp is on or after June 1, 2021.
sql:
SELECT
  event.account_id,
  event.num_events,
  event.num_minutes,
  feature_event.account_id,
  feature_event.num_events,
  page_event.account_id,
  page_event.num_events,
  COALESCE(event.num_events, 0) AS num_events_filled
FROM event
INNER JOIN feature_event ON event.account_id = feature_event.account_id
INNER JOIN page_event ON event.account_id = page_event.account_id
WHERE event.timestamp >= '2021-06-01'

query: For the Pendo visitor event data, please show me the event timestamp, visitor id, event number of events, feature event timestamp, and page event timestamp for each row? Only include rows where the user agent contains 'Firefox' (e.g. Firefox browser), and join so we only see visitors who have matching records in event, feature event, and page event.
sql:
SELECT
  event.timestamp,
  event.visitor_id,
  event.num_events,
  feature_event.timestamp,
  page_event.timestamp
FROM event
INNER JOIN feature_event ON event.visitor_id = feature_event.visitor_id
INNER JOIN page_event ON event.visitor_id = page_event.visitor_id
WHERE event.user_agent LIKE '%Firefox%'

query: From the Pardot data, could you please show me the prospect's industry, state, and country, the campaign name, the opportunity's campaign ID, status, value, and closed date? I'd also like to see the opportunity value per thousand as a ratio. Please include only rows where the opportunity value is not null and greater than zero, and sort the results by this ratio in descending order.
sql:
SELECT
  prospect.industry,
  prospect.state,
  prospect.country,
  campaign.name,
  opportunity.campaign_id,
  opportunity.status,
  opportunity.value,
  opportunity.closed_at,
  CAST(opportunity.value AS REAL) / 1000 AS ratio
FROM campaign
INNER JOIN prospect ON prospect.campaign_id = campaign.id
INNER JOIN opportunity ON opportunity.campaign_id = campaign.id
WHERE opportunity.value IS NOT NULL
  AND CAST(opportunity.value AS REAL) > 0
ORDER BY ratio DESC

query: Retrieve the total number of recipients for each automation in the Mailchimp database, including details such as the automation title, its status, the recipient's action, and the associated URL, grouped by these attributes.
sql: SELECT t2.title AS automation_title, t2.status AS automation_status, t3.action AS recipient_action, t3.url AS recipient_url, COUNT(t3.member_id) AS total_recipients FROM "mailchimp"."automation_email" AS t1 JOIN "mailchimp"."automation" AS t2 ON t2.id = t1.automation_id JOIN "mailchimp"."automation_recipient_activity" AS t3 ON t3.automation_email_id = t1.id  GROUP BY t2.title, t2.status, t3.action, t3.url

query: Retrieve the total delay amount along with the creation time, archive URL, member ID, and list ID from the Mailchimp database, ensuring that any missing delay amounts are considered as zero, and group the information by creation time, archive URL, member ID, and list ID.
sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(t1.delay_amount), 0) AS total_delay_amount, t1.create_time, t1.archive_url, t3.member_id, t3.list_id FROM "mailchimp"."automation_email" AS t1 JOIN "mailchimp"."automation_recipient" AS t3 ON t3.automation_email_id = t1.id GROUP BY t1.create_time, t1.archive_url, t3.member_id, t3.list_id

query: Retrieve the top five opportunities by value, along with their associated companies and email addresses, from the Pardot database, ensuring that these opportunities are ranked highest for each company based on their value.
sql:
WITH cte AS (
    SELECT t2.company, t2.email, t3.value AS opportunity_value, t3.probability,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t2.company ORDER BY t3.value DESC) AS rn
    FROM "pardot"."campaign" AS t1
    JOIN "pardot"."prospect" AS t2 ON t2.campaign_id = t1.id
    JOIN "pardot"."opportunity" AS t3 ON t3.campaign_id = t1.id
)
SELECT company, email, opportunity_value, probability FROM cte WHERE rn <= 5

query: Retrieve the feature name, creation date, agent name, Salesforce customer health engagement score, agent email, and last browser name from the Pendo database for each feature event, along with associated visitor and account details.
sql: SELECT t2.feature_name, t2.created_at, t3.agent_name, t3.salesforce_customer_health_engagement_score_c, t4.agent_email, t4.last_browser_name FROM "pendo"."feature_event" AS t1 JOIN "pendo"."int_pendo__feature_info" AS t2 ON t2.feature_id = t1.feature_id JOIN "pendo"."visitor_history" AS t4 ON t4.id = t1.visitor_id JOIN "pendo"."account_history" AS t3 ON t3.id = t1.account_id

query: Retrieve the production agent version, whether the application is disabled, feature name, feature color, and the average of the dirty flag from the Pendo database, grouped by production agent version, application disabled status, feature name, and feature color.
sql: SELECT t5.agent_version_prod AS production_agent_version, t5.application_flags_disabled AS is_application_disabled, t6.name AS feature_name, t6.color AS feature_color, AVG(t6.dirty::int) AS average_dirty_flag FROM "pendo"."page_history" AS t1 JOIN "pendo"."application_history" AS t5 ON t5.id = t1.app_id JOIN "pendo"."feature_history" AS t6 ON t6.page_id = t1.id GROUP BY t5.agent_version_prod, t5.application_flags_disabled, t6.name, t6.color

query: Retrieve the most recent user who updated each page, including the page ID, page name, user ID, and user's first name, from the Pendo database.
sql:
WITH cte1 AS (
    SELECT t1.id AS page_id, t1.name AS page_name, t2.id AS user_id, t2.first_name,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t1.id ORDER BY t2.id DESC) AS row_num
    FROM "pendo"."page_history" AS t1
    JOIN "pendo"."user" AS t2 ON t2.id = t1.last_updated_by_user_id
),
cte2 AS (
    SELECT page_id, page_name, user_id, first_name FROM cte1 WHERE row_num = 1
)
SELECT * FROM cte2

query: Retrieve the guide name, device type, state, average engagement score, plan level, and payment status for each guide from the Pendo database, grouped by guide name, device type, state, plan level, and payment status.
sql: WITH guide_account_data AS (SELECT t2.guide_name, t2.device_type, t2.state, COUNT(*) AS avg_engagement_score, t3.agent_planlevel, t3.agent_is_paying FROM "pendo"."guide_event" AS t1 JOIN "pendo"."int_pendo__guide_info" AS t2 ON t2.guide_id = t1.guide_id JOIN "pendo"."account_history" AS t3 ON t3.id = t1.account_id GROUP BY t2.guide_name, t2.device_type, t2.state, t3.agent_planlevel, t3.agent_is_paying) SELECT * FROM guide_account_data

query: Retrieve the guide identifiers, step identifiers, and the last updated timestamps of guides from the Pendo database, along with the first names, last names, and roles of the users who last updated them.
sql: SELECT t2.guide_id AS guide_identifier, t2.step_id AS guide_step_identifier, t2.guide_last_updated_at AS guide_last_updated, t4.first_name AS user_first_name, t4.last_name AS user_last_name, t4.role AS user_role FROM "pendo"."guide_history" AS t1 JOIN "pendo"."guide_step_history" AS t2 ON t2.guide_id = t1.id JOIN "pendo"."user" AS t4 ON t4.id = t1.last_updated_by_user_id

query: Retrieve the first name, last name, role, rule, and designer hint of users along with the total count of agent version staging from the Pendo database, grouped by each user's first name, last name, role, rule, and designer hint.
sql: SELECT t2.first_name, t2.last_name, t2.role, t4.rule, t4.designer_hint, COUNT(*) AS total_agent_version_staging FROM "pendo"."page_history" AS t1 JOIN "pendo"."user" AS t2 ON t2.id = t1.last_updated_by_user_id JOIN "pendo"."application_history" AS t5 ON t5.id = t1.app_id JOIN "pendo"."page_rule_history" AS t4 ON t4.page_id = t1.id GROUP BY t2.first_name, t2.last_name, t2.role, t4.rule, t4.designer_hint

query: Retrieve the most recent three features, along with their rules and last update dates, associated with each page from the Pendo database.
sql:
WITH cte AS (
    SELECT t4.page_id, t4.rule, t6.name AS feature_name, t6.last_updated_at,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t4.page_id ORDER BY t6.last_updated_at DESC) AS rn
    FROM "pendo"."page_history" AS t1
    JOIN "pendo"."page_rule_history" AS t4 ON t4.page_id = t1.id
    JOIN "pendo"."feature_history" AS t6 ON t6.page_id = t1.id
)
SELECT page_id, rule, feature_name, last_updated_at FROM cte WHERE rn <= 3

query: Retrieve the account names, their corresponding engagement scores, and visitor emails from the Pendo database, and show the average engagement score for each account, with the data grouped by account name and visitor email.
sql: SELECT t3.agent_name AS account_name, CAST(t3.agent_name AS VARCHAR) AS account_name_casted, t3.salesforce_customer_health_engagement_score_c AS engagement_score, AVG(CAST(t3.salesforce_customer_health_engagement_score_c AS FLOAT)) AS avg_engagement_score, t4.agent_email AS visitor_email, CAST(t4.agent_email AS VARCHAR) AS visitor_email_casted FROM "pendo"."feature_event" AS t1 JOIN "pendo"."visitor_history" AS t4 ON t4.id = t1.visitor_id JOIN "pendo"."account_history" AS t3 ON t3.id = t1.account_id GROUP BY t3.agent_name, t3.salesforce_customer_health_engagement_score_c, t4.agent_email

query: Retrieve the feature names, application IDs, event counts, and visitor IDs from the Pendo database.
sql: SELECT t1.name AS feature_name, t1.app_id, t2.num_events, t2.visitor_id FROM "pendo"."feature_history" AS t1 JOIN "pendo"."feature_event" AS t2 ON t2.feature_id = t1.id

query: Retrieve the most recently updated feature details including feature name and its associated page name from the Pendo database.
sql:
WITH cte1 AS (
    SELECT t1.id AS feature_id, t1.name AS feature_name, t2.name AS page_name,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t2.id ORDER BY t1.last_updated_at DESC) AS row_num
    FROM "pendo"."feature_history" AS t1
    JOIN "pendo"."page_history" AS t2 ON t2.id = t1.page_id
),
cte2 AS (
    SELECT feature_id, feature_name, page_name FROM cte1 WHERE row_num = 1
)
SELECT * FROM cte2

query: Retrieve the average engagement score for each combination of agent name, agent plan level, page name, and app ID from the Pendo database, grouped by these attributes.
sql: SELECT t2.agent_name, t2.agent_planlevel, t3.page_name, t3.app_id, COUNT(*) AS avg_engagement_score FROM "pendo"."page_event" AS t1 JOIN "pendo"."account_history" AS t2 ON t2.id = t1.account_id JOIN "pendo"."int_pendo__page_info" AS t3 ON t3.page_id = t1.page_id GROUP BY t2.agent_name, t2.agent_planlevel, t3.page_name, t3.app_id

query: Retrieve the names and last updated dates of the five most recently updated features for each application from the Pendo database, along with the application names.
sql:
WITH cte AS (
    SELECT t1.name AS feature_name, t1.last_updated_at, t3.display_name AS app_name,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t3.id ORDER BY t1.last_updated_at DESC) AS rn
    FROM "pendo"."feature_history" AS t1
    JOIN "pendo"."application_history" AS t3 ON t3.id = t1.app_id
)
SELECT feature_name, last_updated_at, app_name FROM cte WHERE rn <= 5

query: Retrieve the most recently updated features along with their corresponding pages and applications from the Pendo database, limited to the 10 most recent entries for each application.
sql:
WITH recent_records AS (
    SELECT t1.name AS feature_name, t2.name AS page_name, t3.display_name AS app_name,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t3.id ORDER BY t1.last_updated_at DESC) AS row_num
    FROM "pendo"."feature_history" AS t1
    JOIN "pendo"."page_history" AS t2 ON t2.id = t1.page_id
    JOIN "pendo"."application_history" AS t3 ON t3.id = t1.app_id
)
SELECT feature_name, page_name, app_name FROM recent_records WHERE row_num <= 10

query: Retrieve the list of features along with their corresponding page names from the Pendo database, ensuring that both feature and page names are available.
sql:
WITH cte1 AS (
    SELECT t1.id AS feature_id, t1.name AS feature_name, t1.page_id
    FROM "pendo"."feature_history" AS t1
    WHERE t1.name IS NOT NULL
),
cte2 AS (
    SELECT t2.id AS page_id, t2.name AS page_name
    FROM "pendo"."page_history" AS t2
    WHERE t2.name IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT cte1.feature_id, cte1.feature_name, cte2.page_name
FROM cte1
JOIN cte2 ON cte2.page_id = cte1.page_id

query: Retrieve the timestamp, latitude (defaulting to zero if missing), country, guide ID, and count of engagement scores from the Pendo database, grouped by timestamp, latitude, country, and guide ID to analyze engagement patterns.
sql: SELECT t1.timestamp, COALESCE(t1.latitude, 0) AS latitude, t1.country, t1.guide_id, COUNT(*) AS avg_engagement_score FROM "pendo"."guide_event" AS t1 JOIN "pendo"."account_history" AS t3 ON t3.id = t1.account_id GROUP BY t1.timestamp, t1.latitude, t1.country, t1.guide_id

query: Retrieve the names and colors of pages, along with their application names and display names, and the names of associated features from the Pendo database. Also, find the count of records for each combination where the count is more than one, grouped by page name, color, application name, display name, and feature name.
sql:
SELECT t1.name AS page_name, t1.color, t2.name AS app_name, t2.display_name,
  t5.name AS feature_name, COUNT(*) AS record_count
FROM "pendo"."page_history" AS t1
JOIN "pendo"."application_history" AS t2 ON t2.id = t1.app_id
JOIN "pendo"."feature_history" AS t5 ON t5.page_id = t1.id
GROUP BY t1.name, t1.color, t2.name, t2.display_name, t5.name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

query: Retrieve the average designer hint score for each page from the Pendo database, along with the page ID, page name, production agent version, and related feature name, grouped by page ID, page name, agent version, and feature name.
sql: SELECT t1.id AS page_id, t1.name AS page_name, t5.agent_version_prod AS agent_version, t6.name AS feature_name, AVG(t4.designer_hint::NUMERIC) AS avg_designer_hint FROM "pendo"."page_history" AS t1 JOIN "pendo"."application_history" AS t5 ON t5.id = t1.app_id JOIN "pendo"."feature_history" AS t6 ON t6.page_id = t1.id JOIN "pendo"."page_rule_history" AS t4 ON t4.page_id = t1.id GROUP BY t1.id, t1.name, t5.agent_version_prod, t6.name

query: Retrieve the names of guides, their associated step IDs, and application names from the Pendo database, including the rank of each step, but only for the first five steps of each guide.
sql:
WITH ranked AS (
    SELECT t1.name AS guide_name, t2.step_id, t3.display_name AS app_name,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t1.id ORDER BY t2.step_id) AS step_rank
    FROM "pendo"."guide_history" AS t1
    JOIN "pendo"."guide_step_history" AS t2 ON t2.guide_id = t1.id
    JOIN "pendo"."application_history" AS t3 ON t3.id = t1.app_id
)
SELECT guide_name, step_id, app_name, step_rank FROM ranked WHERE step_rank <= 5

query: Retrieve the account identifier, page identifier, account name, and plan level from the Pendo database, along with the total number of events and the average number of minutes, grouped by account and page.
sql: SELECT t1.account_id AS account_identifier, t1.page_id AS page_identifier, t2.agent_name AS account_name, t2.agent_planlevel AS plan_level, SUM(t1.num_events) AS total_events, AVG(t1.num_minutes) AS average_minutes FROM "pendo"."page_event" AS t1 JOIN "pendo"."account_history" AS t2 ON t2.id = t1.account_id GROUP BY t1.account_id, t1.page_id, t2.agent_name, t2.agent_planlevel

query: Retrieve the total number of events for each feature and account, along with the average duration spent on pages, from the Pendo database, grouped by account and feature.
sql: SELECT t2.account_id, t2.feature_id, SUM(t2.num_events) AS total_feature_events, AVG(t3.num_minutes) AS avg_page_minutes FROM "pendo"."event" AS t1 JOIN "pendo"."page_event" AS t3 ON t3.account_id = t1.account_id JOIN "pendo"."feature_event" AS t2 ON t2.account_id = t1.account_id GROUP BY t2.account_id, t2.feature_id

query: Retrieve the latest three interactions for each visitor from the Pendo database, detailing the timestamp, guide name, agent name, and agent email, along with the count of interactions for each guide.
sql: WITH cte AS (SELECT t1.timestamp, t2.guide_name, t3.agent_name, t4.agent_email, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t1.visitor_id ORDER BY t1.timestamp DESC) AS row_num FROM "pendo"."guide_event" AS t1 JOIN "pendo"."int_pendo__guide_info" AS t2 ON t2.guide_id = t1.guide_id JOIN "pendo"."visitor_history" AS t4 ON t4.id = t1.visitor_id JOIN "pendo"."account_history" AS t3 ON t3.id = t1.account_id) SELECT timestamp, guide_name, agent_name, agent_email, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY guide_name) AS guide_interaction_count FROM cte WHERE row_num <= 3

query: Retrieve the organization tags along with their synchronization dates and associated domain names with their synchronization dates from the Zendesk database.
sql: SELECT t2.tag AS organization_tag, t2._fivetran_synced::DATE AS tag_sync_date, t3.domain_name AS domain_name, t3._fivetran_synced::DATE AS domain_sync_date FROM "zendesk"."organization" AS t1 JOIN "zendesk"."organization_tag" AS t2 ON t2.organization_id = t1.id JOIN "zendesk"."domain_name" AS t3 ON t3.organization_id = t1.id

query: Retrieve the total and average chat index for each brand and priority from the Zendesk database, grouped by brand and priority.
sql: SELECT t1.brand_id, t1.priority, SUM(t5.chat_index) AS total_chat_index, AVG(t5.chat_index) AS average_chat_index FROM "zendesk"."ticket" AS t1 JOIN "zendesk"."ticket_chat" AS t2 ON t2.ticket_id = t1.id JOIN "zendesk"."ticket_chat_event" AS t5 ON t5.chat_id = t2.chat_id GROUP BY t1.brand_id, t1.priority

query: Retrieve the most recent field name and chat message for each ticket from the Zendesk database.
sql: WITH ticket_updates_cte AS (SELECT t3.field_name, t5.message, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t3.ticket_id ORDER BY t3.updated DESC) AS row_num FROM "zendesk"."ticket" AS t1 JOIN "zendesk"."ticket_chat" AS t2 ON t2.ticket_id = t1.id JOIN "zendesk"."ticket_field_history" AS t3 ON t3.ticket_id = t1.id JOIN "zendesk"."ticket_chat_event" AS t5 ON t5.chat_id = t2.chat_id) SELECT field_name, message FROM ticket_updates_cte WHERE row_num = 1

query: Retrieve field names, user IDs, and record counts from the Zendesk database, grouped by field name and user.
sql:
SELECT t3.field_name, t3.user_id, COUNT(*) AS record_count
FROM "zendesk"."ticket" AS t1
JOIN "zendesk"."ticket_field_history" AS t3 ON t3.ticket_id = t1.id
GROUP BY t3.field_name, t3.user_id

query: Retrieve the most recent ticket details from the Zendesk database, including ticket ID, creation date, priority, assignee ID, associated brand URL, and tags, ensuring each ticket's latest information is displayed.
sql: WITH latest_ticket AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t1.id ORDER BY t1.created_at DESC) AS row_num FROM "zendesk"."ticket" AS t1) SELECT t1.id AS ticket_id, t1.created_at, t1.priority, t1.assignee_id, t3.brand_url, t2.tag FROM latest_ticket AS t1 JOIN "zendesk"."brand" AS t3 ON t3.id = t1.brand_id JOIN "zendesk"."ticket_tag" AS t2 ON t2.ticket_id = t1.id WHERE row_num = 1 GROUP BY t1.id, t1.created_at, t1.priority, t1.assignee_id, t3.brand_url, t2.tag;

query: Retrieve the ticket ID, ticket creation date, chat channel, ticket field name, and comment body from the Zendesk database, along with the average user ID for each ticket, grouped by ticket details and comment information.
sql: SELECT t1.id AS ticket_id, CAST(t1.created_at AS DATE) AS ticket_creation_date, t2.channel AS chat_channel, t3.field_name AS ticket_field_name, t4.body AS comment_body, AVG(t4.user_id) AS average_user_id FROM "zendesk"."ticket" AS t1 JOIN "zendesk"."ticket_chat" AS t2 ON t2.ticket_id = t1.id JOIN "zendesk"."ticket_comment" AS t4 ON t4.ticket_id = t1.id JOIN "zendesk"."ticket_field_history" AS t3 ON t3.ticket_id = t1.id GROUP BY t1.id, t1.created_at, t2.channel, t3.field_name, t4.body

query: Retrieve the total chat index, chat ID, user ID, channel, and event message for each chat from the Zendesk database.
sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(t5.chat_index), 0) AS total_chat_index, t2.chat_id, t2.user_id, t2.channel, COALESCE(t5.message, '') AS event_message FROM "zendesk"."ticket_chat" AS t2 JOIN "zendesk"."ticket_chat_event" AS t5 ON t5.chat_id = t2.chat_id GROUP BY t2.chat_id, t2.user_id, t2.channel, t5.message
